reports.title: Georgia’s Tallis Morrison takes lead at the Toyota Series Championship Presented by Phoenix Boats on Pickwick Lake
reports.text:
COUNCE, Tenn. – Given a full day to fish, weights were much improved on Day 2 of the 2026 Toyota Series Championship Presented by Phoenix Boats on Pickwick Lake – especially on the co-angler side, more limits came to the scale where despite the wind, plenty of fish were caught.
Moving up from fourth to take the lead on the pro side, Tallis Morrison of Canon, Georgia, weighed 20 pounds, 2 ounces to get to a two-day total of 39-5. Right behind him, Hayden O’Barr of Scottsboro, Alabama, sacked up 20-7 to move from eighth to second with an even 39 pounds. reports.title: Best Bass Fishing Rods for 2026
reports.text:
The best fishing rod is almost always the one you reach for most — the trusty setup that feels perfectly balanced in your hands and adapts to various techniques on the water. Because every angler’s preferences are shaped by where and how they fish, budget, cosmetics, and comfort, there is no single “perfect” rod that works for everyone. Fortunately, today’s market offers a vast selection of high-quality options tailored to virtually every situation.

reports.title: Wired2fish Head of Video, Tournament Angler Lands “Catch of a Lifetime” 7-Pound Smallmouth
reports.text:
When you’re both an experienced tournament angler and a videographer in the fishing industry, big fish come with the territory. But every once in a while, a fish can still come along that leaves even the most seasoned anglers shaking their heads.
That was the case for Wired2fish Head of Video Nick Dumke on Nov. 1, when he landed an incredible 7-pound smallmouth bass on Minnesota’s Mille Lacs Lake.
Dumke, a tournament angler who has spent years pursuing bass across a variety of fisheries, has long admired the giant smallmouth that Mille Lacs produces. With several impressive fish coming from the lake over the past couple of years, catching one of those true giants had become a personal goal…

reports.title: Best Rod and Reel Combos for 2026
reports.text: For anglers seeking simplicity, a rod-and-reel combo is the ultimate grab-and-go solution. These combos are often aimed at travelers who want to be prepped for spontaneous fishing opportunities on a road trip. Many combos have a rod that breaks down into at least two pieces, although some are one-piece. I used to walk the aisles of sporting goods stores looking for deals on spin combos as a kid. I still do, but I used to, too. Some of those setups I grabbed at bargain prices lasted for years. In fact, I still have some combos in my rotation right now. reports.title: Anglers caught quality largemouth bass around submerged trees, main lake points, and the dam
reports.text: The lake level remained low at approximately 10% of its storage capacity, while bass fishing was good. Anglers caught quality largemouth bass around submerged trees, main lake points, and the dam in 10 to 25 feet of water. Some of the larger bass were caught on 8- and 10-inch worms and crankbaits fished near submerged trees. Crappie reports were limited, but anglers found good-quality fish near submerged vegetation, with small live minnows and mini jigs producing the best results.

reports.title: The lake level remained low
reports.text: The lake level remained low at approximately 10% of its storage capacity, while fishing for spotted bass improved. Crappie were found holding near submerged stick-ups, and rocks in 15 to 25 feet of water, with small live minnows producing the best results, particularly around Horse Creek, although smaller swimbaits also caught fish.

reports.title: Fishing was productive for aqueduct anglers in the Bakersfield area
reports.text: Largemouth bass were caught on drop-shot rigs with six-inch straight-tailed worms, with darker colors producing the best results.

reports.text:
There’s nothing wrong with being a bass fisherman. According to Smithwick Associates, there are about 11 million of them in the US, though that number expands out to about 30 million depending on how casual participation is defined. reports.title: Inaugural WBE Tournament Declares Winner, Delivers Pro Bass Fishing’s Biggest Payout Yet
reports.text:
With the Nov. 1 conclusion of World Bass Enterprises ’ (WBE’s) “The Champions” tournament comes the crowning of a brand-new winner. Matt Robertson claimed not only the first-place spot but also the largest monetary prize ever awarded in a professional bass fishing tournament — $1.25 million.
“It’s freaking insane, I don’t think it’s really hit me yet. I just won the biggest tournament ever in bass fishing,” said Robertson, a resident of Kuttawa, Kentucky. “$1.25 million will drastically change my life… This was an awesome experience, this is the Super Bowl of bass fishing.”

reports.title: Thankfulness: so much to be thankful for
reports.text:
Cooler temperatures are just one reason to be thankful
N ovember is a month I’m thankful to see roll around every year. The cooler temperatures and frosty mornings are a reprieve from the intense heat domes we’ve suffered through these past summers. July and August triple-digit readings have forced me to sweat profusely instead of lightly perspiring. It’s wonderful to stand in cold water, chilled, and try to catch a trout on a fly. Exhaling slowly, I watch my damp breath turn into ice crystals and disappear. What a beautiful morning to be here. Quiet, alone, and time to ponder the things I’ve been too busy to think about otherwise.

reports.title: CN How To Nov 2026 How To: Crappie Dan explains how shadows, current, and underwater structure influence crappie behavior.
reports.text:
How To: Crappie Dan explains how shadows, current, and underwater structure influence crappie behavior.
In this episode of The Playbook, Crappie Dan explains how shadows, current, and underwater structure influence crappie and bass behavior. Fish often face into the current, positioning themselves where baitfish will naturally approach. During sunny conditions, they tend to hold in the shade created by stumps, brush, overhanging trees, and shoreline drop-offs, often near the edge of the light.
The key to success is proper boat positioning and bait placement. When casting or jigging, position your bait up current so it moves naturally toward the fish. Approaching from behind can spook them…

reports.title: Hit Lake Murray’s brush for fall crappie
reports.text:
Don’t miss the fall crappie bite
A s Lake Murray’s water temperature cools down in October, Capt. Brad Taylor of Taylor Outdoors said the crappie fishing gets cranked up.
“October is a great month because you can catch crappie in a number of ways, really just about any way you want to catch them will work,” he said.
One way Taylor targets them this time of year is by fishing brush in the main river channel.
“Fall is kind of a magical time of year for Lake Murray because the shad start working up the river,” he said. “And the crappie follow the bait. If you can find the bait, which isn’t too difficult using electronics, then you can find the crappie.”

reports.text:
Matching your jig to the size and shape of the main crappie forage can greatly increase your number of hookups.
Crappie Basics: Match the Hatch for More Crappie
By Keith Sutton
One of the simplest ways to improve your crappie fishing is to give the fish what they’re already looking for. That means matching your jig to the size and general shape of the forage crappie are feeding on.
If 2-inch minnows make up a big part of the crappie diet in the lake you’re fishing, for example, a 2-inch jig is a logical choice. If the fish are eating tiny shiners, you’ll probably do better with a smaller offering. The same principle applies when shad, fathead minnows or other forage dominate the menu.
